This appeal coming on for admission this day, th e court passed the following:
 ORDER

Appellants/owner & driver of the offending vehicle has filed this appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 assailing the award dated 31/10/2018 passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhind in Claims case No. 39/2017; whereby, respondents No. 1 to 5/claimants have been awarded a compensation of Rs.7,45,000/- for the death of one Narendra Singh Sikh in road accident dated 30/10/2015.
2.

Briefly stated facts of the case are that on 30/10/2015 when deceased Narendra Singh Sikh (husband of respondent No. 1 and father of respondents no. 2 to 5) was travelling in Bolero Loading Max MP07GA1972 from Ater to Bhind, it is alleged that due to rash and negligent driving of appellant No. 2 the vehicle turned turtle, due to which Narenda Singh sustained grievous hurts therefore, he was taken to District Hospital Bhind from where he was referred to J.A.Hospital,
Gwalior where he succumbed to the injuries on 4/11/2015.

Therefore, claimants filed a claim case before the Claims Tribunal seeking total compensation of Rs. 41,70,000/-; however, by the impugned award, Claims Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs. 7,45,000/- alongwith interest at the rate of 7% per annum from the date of application.

The liability for payment of compensation was fastened over appellants/owner and driver of the offending vehicle while exonerating the Insurance Company on the ground that the offending vehicle was being plied in breach of insurance policy.
Thus, owner and driver of the offending vehicle is before this Court challenging the liability part of the impugned award.

3. It is the submission of learned senior counsel for the appellants that there was no evidence that accident was caused by their vehicle as there are material contradictions and omissions in the evidence of claimants.

Further learned Claims Tribunal erred in holding that the vehicle was being plied in breach of Insurance Policy as the deceased was travelling in the vehicle alongwith his goods and therefore, cannot be said to be a passenger.

It is further submitted that in light of decision of Apex Court in the matter of Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., 2017 ACJ 2011,
learned Claims Tribunal erred in holding that appellant No. 2 was not holding valid driving licence to drive the offending vehicle.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondents supported the impugned award and prayed for dismissal of the appeal.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties at length and perused the record.
6.
This is an appeal by the owner of the offending vehicle.
It is not in dispute that the appellant No. 2 has caused the death of deceased Narendra Singh by negligently driving the vehicle due to which the vehicle turned turtle.
It is also an admitted fact that at the time of accident the deceased was travelling in this vehicle and the vehicle was insured with respondent No.6-Insurace Company.
On perusal of the Insurance policy, Ex. D/1, the vehicle in question is registered as a goods vehicle and is insured as such by the respondent company.
The sitting capacity of the vehicle is only for one person that is driver.
7. It is submitted by the appellants that the deceased was travelling in the vehicle alongwith his goods and not as passenger for transportation of his goods.
But in this regard no reliable evidence is available on record.
Hence, it cannot be assumed that the deceased was travelling alongwith his goods in the vehicle and was not a passenger.
8. It is settled law that passengers cannot travel in the goods vehicle.
Even gratuitous passengers are not allowed to travel in the goods vehicle.

As per the Insurance Policy (Ex.D-1), besides the driver and cleaner, the risk of no other occupant of the vehicle has been covered nor any premium has been paid by the owner (appellant) for the purpose.
Hence, even if it is assumed for a while that the deceased was travelling alongwith his goods, even then no liability can be fastened on the Insurance Company for the payment of compensation.

9. Further as regards decision of Apex Court in the matter of Mukund Dewangan (supra), from perusal of impugned order it is clear that Claims Tribunal has exonerated the Insurance Company from its liablity not only on the ground that driver of offending vehicle was not holding the valid driving licence alone but also on the ground that deceased was travelling in the vehicle in the capacity of passenger also, therefore, this contention of learned senior counsel for the appellants has no force to effect the merits of the impugned award.

10. In view of the above, it is clear that the Tribunal has rightly found that the deceased was a passenger in the goods vehicle and hence the offending vehicle was being driven by appellant No. 2 in violation of policy conditions.
The risk of the deceased is also not covered under the policy.
As a consequence, the Tribunal has rightly exonerated the Insurance Company from its liability to pay the compensation.
11. Appeal sans merits, hence dismissed.
(ROOPESH CHANDRA VARSHNEY)

JUDGE JPS/-
